He achieves good health by a wise doctor, who gives him one remedy to drink that causes his purulent sickness to break out above, and gives him another medicine to drink that causes his sickness to discharge below, and he gives him yet another medicine to drink that cures his wounds for him [and purifies him] calmly and silently.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading indicates the three containing forms existed within the rulers before being expelled; ¶5 explicitly says these vessels "are hidden in the body of all the rulers above," so "were hidden" is the natural-register vocabulary for this initial state.

A standard Kephalaia transitional formula introducing an exposition; the sentence moves from the chapter's topic statement to the specific description of "the manner in which the three vessels have been discharged."

The spiritual reading specifies "violent spiritual destruction"; in the Kephalaia's register, "great" is the standard intensifier for "slaughter," yielding "great slaughter" for the violent discharge of the vessels.

The spiritual reading says "separated these containing forms from them"; "who separated" introduces the agents (the Living Spirit and his garments) and echoes ¶1's vocabulary of "discharged and separated."

The third medicine works gently, contrasting with the first two that violently purge above and below; "and purifies him" adds a general cleansing action alongside the specific wound-cure, matching the spiritual reading's emphasis on gentle restoration.

The spiritual reading introduces a new clause after the healers' action; "heal, and" provides the main verb for "the doctors shall heal" and connects to the elaborating clause "they work cures through the aroma."

The spiritual reading says "other distortions [in] what is concealed within"; the wounds are located within the hidden parts of the body, requiring forceful extraction — "that are in" establishes their deep concealment before "they at last tear them out."
The hidden wounds are torn out from within the body and then made visible; "within, and are" connects the extraction from their concealed location to their manifestation "above and below."

The spiritual reading confirms "through the perception of truths received and applied"; "and purified through" completes the healing sequence — manifested and then purified through the aroma of edible medicines — with "through" being the surviving fragment at the gap's edge.

fills.original: ... / ... in the womb of his mother. His mother also is just like
fills.explanation: The child must have exactly 9 garments to total 18 with the mother's 9; only 7 body layers are listed, so the gap must name the 8th (an inner covering/membrane around the child) and the 9th (the womb itself that encloses the child), leading into the surviving text "in the womb of his mother."

The child is the active agent who opens up the coverings to emerge; "it" is the pronoun for the child in the womb, consistent with the later statement "it emerges from a crack" and "this child opens up the womb of his mother."
The text explicitly states later "this child opens up the womb of his mother"; the same verb "open up" applies to the child opening all the coverings/garments to emerge at birth.
The editor's choice fits: "these things" refers to all eighteen garments/coverings the child must open to emerge, and the spiritual reading confirms "these things" at this position.

fills.fill: in which he was revealed to them, he shook them and discharged the vessel of water
fills.explanation: The parallel structure of ¶9 and ¶10 strongly constrains this medium gap: each garment is used to reveal the Living Spirit to the rulers and discharge the corresponding vessel; "shook them" echoes ¶5's "with shaking and fear" and ¶7's birth-shaking imagery.

The Living Spirit moved the waters out of the rulers; "for" introduces the explanation that these waters "are the poison and death with which their veins and entrails are filled," identifying what was discharged.

The Living Spirit was revealed "to them" (the rulers), exactly paralleling the pattern in ¶5 ("displayed to the rulers") and the reconstructed ¶8; the garment of wind was the means of revelation to the rulers before sweeping away darkness.

The chapter consistently uses "cast down" for the descent of vessels to earth (¶10: "threw it down," ¶17: "cast down to the earth"); "and cast them" connects the stripping of garments to their descent, using the text's established vocabulary.

The Kephalaia consistently reinforces directional descent with doubling ("down to the earth below"); "below" concludes ¶11's description of the garments being cast downward, matching the chapter's established pattern of directional emphasis.

The list "creations, trees, all flesh" appears repeatedly in the chapter (¶16, ¶17, ¶19); "for" transitions to the explanation of how the evil was contained in three things, matching the spiritual reading's threefold containment.

The editor's reading is confirmed: the passage describes what would have happened if the vessel of water had not been swept down, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "containing form of falsified truth" — water being the natural-register term for falsified truth throughout this chapter.

The parallel passage in ¶17 uses "flow down from above to the earth" for torrents; "down" completes the phrase "torrents that would flow down" in perfect parallel with the established pattern of descent.

The parallel in ¶17 explicitly uses "drops of darkness, which will drip down"; "drip" is the text's own verb for the action of droplets descending, creating exact structural parallelism between ¶16 and ¶17.

The parallel passages in ¶17 and ¶19 both use "would have multiplied" as the key consequence; "and multiplied" extends the verb chain from "sprouted" to "multiplied," echoing the chapter's consistent vocabulary for the proliferation of evil.

The parallel in ¶17 uses "again" to introduce the conditional consequence of what would have happened if the vessel had not been removed; "again" marks the third iteration of this parallel counterfactual structure.

Strongly constrained by the parallel structure in ¶16-17 where torrents "flow down from above"; for fire, "would have poured down from above" describes the same counterfactual descent, completing the sentence "this fire would have poured down from above through the torrent."
The editor's reading is confirmed: the sequential enumeration of twelve deeds places this as the third deed, between the second (¶21) and the fourth (¶23), describing relief from heavenly burden.
The heavens and firmaments had their burden removed; "and were" connects "burden" to "relieved" as a coordinate clause — the heavens bore a burden and were relieved from the weight-carriers.

The greatness and richness that dwells in the ships actively fills them with divine presence; "as it fills them, you might find them purified and holy" expresses how the indwelling divine abundance produces the state of purification described.

Following the consistent pattern of deed introductions using purpose clauses ("That they might purify," "That great enclosures," etc.), "That the" introduces the seventh deed's purpose regarding the nature of the vessels advancing to their places.

The apostles (divine truths sent forth) go out to the vessels at the edges of the worlds; "reach" describes their arrival before they "return to the universe and give a sign," completing the outward-and-return mission pattern.

The doublet "the end and the dissolution" is a standard eschatological pairing in Manichaean teaching; the apostles give a sign of both the end (telos) and the dissolution (katalysis) of the universe as two aspects of the final consummation.

The tenth deed describes the vessels becoming "releasers and purifiers of everything at the end of the universe"; the fire that burns "all things" completes the simile of total eschatological purification consistent with the Manichaean Great Fire.

Following the established pattern of deed introductions with purpose clauses ("That they would become," "That great enclosures," "That you might find"), "That they" introduces the eleventh deed's purpose of crossing over.

The eleventh deed describes the final separation: the light elements cross to the light realm while the ruling-power is cast to the outer land; "to the light" names the destination of the crossing, contrasting with "the outer land" for the darkness.

The ruling-power is sent to the outer land; "shall be cast out" uses the chapter's established vocabulary for expulsion (¶17: "cast outside the region of the worlds") and connects grammatically to "to the outer land" that follows.

The aeons of light are outside "it" (the entire building surrounded by the wall of fire, mentioned in ¶32), dwelling "in" the place of peace; "it, in" connects the aeons' position beyond the created universe to their dwelling in the realm of peace.

Rest and peace are a standard doublet in the Kephalaia; "the place of rest and of peace" forms the first in the list of descriptors, echoing ¶25's emphasis on rest reaching and purifying the heavenly temples, and matching the correspondential sense of heavenly peace as the cessation of spiritual conflict.

The wall of fire hides the unclean things from the aeons of light who dwell outside; the unclean things "are displayed only in its interior" — within the enclosed space of the universe, invisible to those beyond the wall.

The Kephalaia regularly uses doublets for divine attributes; "great power and authority" is a standard pairing that emphasizes the sovereign dominion of the watching powers set over the confined vessels.
